blind_target.authors: Bateson M, Nettle D, Roberts G.
blind_target.title: Cues of being watched enhance cooperation in a real-world setting.
blind_target.evidence_quote: Based on [21] and [22] we have chosen eyes as prosocial primes, and flowers as a neutral control prime.
blind_target.outcome_quote: What we may conclude, therefore, is that the effect of eye primes on prosocial behavior does not generalize from the settings used by Haley and Fessler [21] and Bateson, Nettles, and Roberts [22]. Our failure to find an effect is informative about the actual overall effect size, and the conditions in which it occurs [32].
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly judge both studies’ eye-prime effect not to generalize to this new sample. They call the null result informative; their inability to rule out the phenomenon in all contexts is not a verdict that this particular test is uninformative.

luna_triage.reason: The discussion explicitly says the study's eye-prime effect does not generalize from the settings of Haley and Fessler and Bateson et al. The methods also state that eyes were selected as prosocial primes based on both studies, and the current study tests whether eye primes affect prosocial giving in a new dictator-game setting. The supplied shipped row represents Haley and Fessler only; Bateson et al. is a separate original work.
